archetypes.name: harness-literal-match
archetypes.rationale: The plan asserts specific harness contracts (PATH_PREFIX stub mechanism, adjacent-pair arg detection, exact error-message strings, variable names like CACHE_REMOVED) that must match the actual source — a mismatch here would silently pass tests for the wrong reason or cause the new case to fail to compile/run.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify every concrete claim the plan makes about the test harness by reading the actual source files rather than trusting the plan's description. Specifically: confirm the PATH_PREFIX stub injection mechanism exists in test-cleanup.sh and works exactly as described (not just for pgrep but for find); confirm the adjacent-pair -maxdepth 5 detection logic is correct bash for the stub; confirm the exact error-message string 'failed to scan session activity' is what cleanup.sh actually emits on find failure (not a paraphrase); confirm CACHE_REMOVED is an actual counter variable the harness exposes; and confirm the unset PATH_PREFIX teardown pattern matches how other stub cases clean up. If any literal diverges from the actual source, flag it as a plan defect — the new test case would either fail to run or pass vacuously. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: doc-scope-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims exactly six stale documentation sites describe the old top-level-mtime-only retention model; a missed site would leave the doc drift unrepaired and the Edit-in-sync trigger misaligned, defeating half the plan's stated purpose.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the plan's enumerated documentation sites (SECURITY.md, cleanup.md, docs/configuration-and-permissions.md, SKILL.md, docs/skills.md, docs/linting.md) are exhaustive. Search the scope files and any cross-referenced docs for additional occurrences of the old retention description — phrases like 'top-level mtime', 'entry's own mtime', or 'find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ... -mtime' — that the plan did not list. Also verify that the plan's proposed replacement wording is internally consistent across all six files: the depth-5 tradeoff sentence, the fail-open wording for enumeration failures, and the fail-safe wording for the nested scan must say the same thing in each doc rather than subtly contradicting each other. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
